summary:
Nova - The Little Astronaut Hero is an educational game app for kids aged 6 to 10. Our idea is to make the child himself the hero. The child puts his own photo in the app and becomes the astronaut. He sees himself inside the Moon base wearing the astronaut suit.

Every day, he gets a new Daily Space Challenge about life on the Moon, like how to fix oxygen, save water, or grow plants without soil. He must think and solve the problem to pass. A friendly robot called Nova helps him. If he is wrong, Nova says let's try again and gives a hint. At the end, Nova asks: What did you learn today?

Our special idea is Nova's Real Mission. After the Moon challenge, Nova gives the child a real mission at home. If the challenge was about water, his mission is to close the tap while brushing teeth. His parent confirms it and he gets double points. So what he learns on the Moon, he does on Earth.

Benefits: kids love science, learn problem-solving, learn good habits, and feel confident. We used Figma for design, Canva for characters, and HTML, CSS, JavaScript for the prototype, and we plan to build it with Flutter. Our project is creative because the child is the hero with his real photo and real mission. We considered age, safety with no ads or strangers chat, parents follow-up, and real NASA facts in every challenge.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Nova is an
educational game app for kids aged 6 to 10. The child puts his own photo in the
app and becomes the astronaut hero. Every day he gets a new challenge about
life on the Moon, like how to fix oxygen, save water, or grow plants. He solves
the problem, gets points, and moves to a new level. A friendly robot called
Nova helps him with hints. After the Moon challenge, Nova gives him a real
mission at home, like saving water while brushing his teeth, and his parent
confirms it.

 

What benefits does
it have?

It makes kids love
science and space. It teaches them problem solving and how to think. It teaches
them good habits in real life like saving water and energy. It also makes them
feel confident because they see themselves as heroes.

 

What is the
intended impact of the project?

We want kids to
stop just watching videos about space and start living the experience. We want
them to think like real astronauts and to connect what they learn on the Moon
with their life on Earth. Our goal is to create a new generation that loves
science and can solve real problems.

 

What tools, coding
languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We used Figma to
design the app screens, Canva to make the characters and visuals, and Google
Docs to write the story. For the game logic we used basic HTML, CSS, and
JavaScript for the prototype, and we plan to build the final app with Flutter
so it works on Android and iPhone.

 

How is your
project creative?

Our creativity is
that the child is the hero, not a cartoon. We use his real photo and his real
name. We also connect the Moon with Earth with the Real Mission idea. The child
learns on the Moon and does the mission in his home. No other app for kids does
this mix of game, personal photo, and real-life mission.

 

What factors did
your team consider?

We considered the
age of the kids, so we made the design simple, colorful, with big buttons and
easy words. We considered safety, so there are no ads and no chatting with
strangers. We considered parents, so they can follow the progress and confirm
the missions. And we considered learning, so every challenge has a real scientific
fact about the Moon.
